topics.title: What finance is
topics.technical: Finance is the management of money over time under uncertainty: how individuals, companies and markets allocate capital, price risk and make decisions today about uncertain tomorrows. Its core question is always value.
topics.simple: Managing money over time — deciding today with an uncertain future in mind.

topics.title: Time value of money
topics.technical: A rupee today is worth more than a rupee tomorrow; present and future value, discounting and compounding formalise this. It underlies every valuation, loan and investment decision in finance.
topics.simple: Money now beats money later — the single idea behind almost all of finance.

topics.title: Interest and compounding
topics.technical: Simple and compound interest, and the frequency of compounding, drive how money grows or debt balloons. Compounding is the quiet engine behind both wealth and ruinous debt.
topics.simple: How money grows on itself — the force behind both savings and crushing debt.

topics.title: Financial statements
topics.technical: The income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement together describe a company's performance, position and liquidity. Reading all three — and how they connect — is financial literacy's core.
topics.simple: The three reports that tell you how a company is really doing.

topics.title: Reading the balance sheet
topics.technical: Assets equal liabilities plus equity; the balance sheet is a snapshot of what a company owns and owes. Its structure reveals solvency and how the business is financed.
topics.simple: A snapshot of what a company owns, owes, and is worth right now.

topics.title: Income and cash flow
topics.technical: Profit is an opinion; cash is a fact. The income statement shows earnings while the cash flow statement shows the money actually moving — profitable companies still fail when cash runs out.
topics.simple: Earnings can be dressed up; cash flow shows the money that truly moved.

topics.title: Financial ratios
topics.technical: Liquidity, profitability, leverage and efficiency ratios turn statements into comparable signals; trends and peer comparison matter more than any single number. Ratios are questions, not verdicts.
topics.simple: Quick measures that turn financial reports into comparable health signals.

topics.title: Risk and return
topics.technical: Higher expected return demands higher risk; measuring risk (volatility, downside) and pricing it is finance's central bargain. Free lunches do not survive in efficient markets.
topics.simple: You cannot get more reward without accepting more risk — finance's basic trade.

topics.title: Diversification and portfolios
topics.technical: Combining uncorrelated assets reduces risk without proportionally cutting return — the one genuinely free lunch. Portfolio thinking beats betting everything on a single conviction.
topics.simple: Not putting all your eggs in one basket — the closest thing to free safety.

topics.title: Stocks and equity markets
topics.technical: Shares represent ownership; markets price them continuously on expectations of future cash flows. Understanding what a share is, and what moves its price, is investing's foundation.
topics.simple: Owning slices of companies — and what makes their prices move.

topics.title: Bonds and fixed income
topics.technical: Bonds are loans with fixed payments; price moves inversely to interest rates, and credit risk sets yield. Fixed income anchors portfolios and reveals the market's view of risk and rates.
topics.simple: Lending money for steady interest — and why bond prices fall when rates rise.

topics.title: Valuation fundamentals
topics.technical: Value is the present value of future cash flows; DCF, multiples and comparables estimate it under uncertainty. Every price is an implicit forecast — valuation makes the forecast explicit.
topics.simple: What is something really worth — the discounted value of the cash it will make.

topics.title: Corporate finance
topics.technical: Companies decide how to raise capital (debt vs equity), which projects to fund, and how to return cash. Capital structure and investment decisions shape value and risk.
topics.simple: How companies decide where to get money and where to spend it.

topics.title: Capital budgeting
topics.technical: NPV, IRR and payback evaluate whether projects create value; positive-NPV decisions grow the firm, and the discount rate encodes risk. It is time value of money applied to real decisions.
topics.simple: Deciding which projects are worth doing by whether they add value.

topics.title: Financial markets and instruments
topics.technical: Equities, bonds, derivatives and currencies trade in interconnected markets that price and transfer risk. Understanding the instruments and who uses them maps how capital actually flows.
topics.simple: The different things that trade — and how markets move risk around.

topics.title: Derivatives basics
topics.technical: Options, futures and swaps derive value from underlying assets and let users hedge or speculate on risk. Powerful and dangerous, they amplify both protection and mistakes.
topics.simple: Contracts that let you bet on or protect against price moves — powerful and risky.

topics.title: Personal finance
topics.technical: Budgeting, saving, debt management, insurance and long-term investing apply finance to a life; compounding and discipline beat cleverness. The principles that build institutional wealth build personal wealth too.
topics.simple: Using finance to manage your own money — budget, save, invest, protect.

topics.title: Behavioral finance
topics.technical: People are not rational: biases like loss aversion, herding and overconfidence move markets and wreck individual decisions. Knowing your own wiring is part of investing well.
topics.simple: Why people — and markets — make predictably irrational money choices.

topics.title: Financial modelling
topics.technical: Spreadsheet models project statements, value companies and test scenarios; clean structure and honest assumptions separate insight from garbage. A model is only as good as its inputs and logic.
topics.simple: Building spreadsheets that forecast and value — only as smart as their assumptions.

topics.title: Ethics and regulation
topics.technical: Finance runs on trust: disclosure, fiduciary duty and regulation exist because the incentives to cheat are enormous. Ethical lapses in finance scale into crises.
topics.simple: Finance depends on trust — and the rules that exist because money tempts.

topics.title: The capstone
topics.technical: Analyse a real company end to end: read its statements, compute ratios, value it, and write an investment view with the reasoning. A full analysis demonstrates financial literacy applied.
topics.simple: Fully analyse and value a real company — proof you can do finance.
